releases.name: shadps4 v0.21.0 - codename Until Mavethee Dawn
releases.body:
Another week another release . There are ton of changes , so why not ? 

## Core
* Properly check where an input came from for digital->analog input smoothing
* cpu_patches: Work around Rosetta 2 mistranslating negated scalar compares 
* file_sys: Report stable file identities in stat and fstat 
* Allow file type identification for '/addcont' path
* emulator: stop clearing temporary data on boot 
* Add PT_SCE_MODULE_PARAM case
* cpu_patches: Fix JIT patching at addresses outside any module
* core: Fix MemoryManager::Free unmapping past the released rang
* file_sys: don't abort when a guest path goes through a regular file
* use VMA pointers instead of copies in TryWriteBacking 
* cpu_patches: Workaround Rosetta 2 crash on VMASKMOVPS/PD
* Handle ELF metadata and toolchain comments program headers
* common: reuse one high-resolution waitable timer per thread in AccurateSleep
* Don't abort when optional ELF metadata segments can't be read
* cpu_patches: Fix register clobbering in Rosetta 2 VMASKMOV workaround 
* renderdoc: Add library name for macOS
* renderdoc: Add alternate path for macOS 
* lru_cache: Fix early stop in ForEachItemBelow 
* Avoid deadlock when Shutdown is re-entered

That was close wasn't it? I know you are not used to so close releases but we have a lot of new things to demonstrate so why not? This release is following the first official stable release of shadNet 0.1.0, so we have some online playability available (yes Bloodborne fans, online Bloodborne is now officially available). There are also a tons of fixes to different areas of emu , you can check the list below. The release is dedicated to our friend Stephen, who is taking a break from shadPS4 due of his studies. Stephen if you are reading this we already miss you ;/

## Core
* cpu_patches: Apply comprehensive SSE4a CPU patches on macOS 
* Shutdown NpHandler before restarting
* cpu_patches: Enable static patching on Linux
* cpu_patches: Patch (V)RCPPS and (V)RSQRTPS on Intel
* Speed up game ID resolution
* Anchor the FPS counter at startup and refactor counter movement check
* address_space: Restore protections after splitting a mapped region on Windows
* kernel: Implement POSIX file attribute and sync APIs
* file_sys: Normalize guest paths and fix mount matching
* Do not expand host mmap range during POSIX AddressSpace::Unmap
* Advance the source pointer for each backing run in TryWri

releases.name: shadps4 v0.19.0 - codename The Shadoween special
releases.body:
Welcome back to another shadPS4 release . It is over one month since our previous release and guess what we are back again with a lot more fixes and a lot more playable games . Rapid work has been done in different areas of the emu, but i guess the glory goes to the huge amount of GPU fixes that improved so many games, some of them are really playable now . I won't steal the fun of discovering these, so here is a brief list of changes.

### Core
- Rewrote signal emulation again 
- Fixed incorrect error return on attempting to create a file in a nonexistent folder in a writable mount 
- Fix reserved region coalescing in POSIX address space code 
- Support loading entitlements from RIF licenses 
- Optimized logger by replacing hash map with table lookup and hide implementation details 
- Support loading DLC as ZAR 
- Reworked slot vector 
- Fixed sceKernelReserveVirtualRange alignment and add ClearName 

### Libraries
- Use present scheduler for blank frame prepare 
- np_auth : Change default GetAuthorizationCode returns to be valid 
- np_trophy: Fixed displaying of trophy name 
- http2 : Fixes and cleanups
- np_tss : Added TSS support
- camera : Use a system mapping for camera frame

Hello there, it hasn't been a while, has it? While not much time has passed since our last stable release, we are here again with a brand new one. The main reason for this release is broken shadNet authorization in certain cases on the 0.17.0 release, but we have some more interesting new features as well.

Firstly, after some fixes, AvPlayer can now be loaded as LLE, meaning that you need the `libSceAvPlayer.sprx` (and `libSceAvPlayerStreaming.sprx`) module(s), which makes broken videos in a few games now work properly.

releases.body:
# Bloodborne PC 1.9.8.1

A fix for seamless co-op on top of 1.9.8.

## Fixed
- **Seamless co-op starts again with mods whose event files hold an empty event.** It stopped with "Making the co-op event files failed" (`event ...: its 0 instructions at -1 are outside the instruction table`). Event files written by mod tools can store an event with no instructions this way; the game reads nothing there, and now the co-op event patcher accepts them too.

The launcher makes the co-op event files again by itself on the next seamless start.

## Credits
Seamless co-op is **BBSC: Yharnam Together** by **[CLSAMG22](https://github.com/CLSAMG22)**: https://github.com/CLSAMG22/BBSC. This port runs BBSC's game files, co-op event patcher and HUD with its own engine and launcher, under BBSC's GPL-2.0 licence. BBSC's source is on its release page; this port's change to its event patcher is listed in `seamless\bbport-seamless.txt`. Thank you, CLSAMG22!

The source of this port's seamless engine (`bin\bb-probe-seamless.exe`) is attached to the 1.9.8 release.

releases.name: Bloodborne for Windows 1.9.6: online connection fix
releases.body:
A small update to 1.9.5 that fixes online play failing to connect on some PCs.

**Installing:** the launcher offers this update by itself. Or unpack it over 1.9.5 (or into a new, empty folder). Your settings and saves stay, and your shader cache is kept: no rebuild this time.

## Fixed
- **"Failed to connect to Bloodborne server. Returning to title menu." at Play Online on some PCs.** The log showed `certificate is not trusted by Windows either (error 0x1)` or `SSL server verification failed`, and trying again usually worked. The port now carries Let's Encrypt's root certificates (ISRG Root X1, X2, YE and YR) itself, so it trusts SuperMedo Server and The Hunter's Dream even on PCs where Windows hasn't downloaded them yet. And when its own check still fails, Windows' check now gets the server's whole certificate chain instead of only its first certificate, which could lead Windows to an expired certificate (that was the 0x1).

releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.2 Public Hotfix 1

This maintenance release hardens the Vulkan and Android runtime introduced in
0.6.2. It keeps the same public feature line and concentrates on conservative
driver compatibility, reusable caches, memory stability and correct platform
scheduling.

## Vulkan compatibility and cache stability

- Added `vulkan_extended_dynamic_state=auto|static|dynamic` globally and per
  game. `auto` uses the faster Vulkan 1.3 path on capable Qualcomm and Mesa
  drivers, while proprietary Mali and Samsung/Xclipse drivers retain the
  established static path until their exact GPU and driver combination has
  been physically validated.
- Explicit `dynamic` mode still falls back safely when the complete required
  Vulkan functionality is unavailable. PanVK and other Mesa drivers are not
  confused with proprietary drivers from the same GPU vendor.
- Host pipeline descriptions are now isolated between static and dynamic
  modes. Vulkan binary caches are additionally separated by the driver's
  pipeline-cache identity and version, preventing incompatible data from being
  reused after a driver, mode or application update.
- Pipeline-cache writes are atomic and periodical

releases.body:
What's new in 0.78

For players
- **32-bit devices:** one APK now holds both ARMv8 (arm64-v8a) and ARMv7
  (armeabi-v7a). Android picks the right one on install, so 64-bit devices
  always run the 64-bit version. OpenGL ES 3.0 is still required.
- **Screen orientation:** the setting now applies to the launcher as well as
  the game and takes effect at once. Auto respects the system rotation lock.
- **Sound:** the audio buffer margin now adapts to the device.
- **Launcher:** new Advanced screen with a Debug mode switch. With it off,
  nothing is written to the log.
- **Logs:** new screen under Data to export, share or send logs to the
  developer, or clear them.

Under the hood
- **Most of the game is now ported C++:** - game code is moving from recompiled to ported native ARM code.
- **Old processor code removed:** x87 emulation is gone from the generated
  code, and the whole game runs in 24-bit floating point. MMX, CPU detection
  and the Pentium FDIV workarounds are removed too.

Known limits
- ARMv7 has only been tested in the 32-bit mode of a 64-bit phone, not on a
  real 32-bit device, so speed on older hardware is unknown.
- Network play is not compatible anymore with PC Mod

- **Keep what you need:** select Base, Updates and DLC independently. Choices appear after inspection, only for content present in your source. Latest-snapshot mode merges the newest selected update with the selected base, retains required base-only files, and leaves superseded versions behind. - **NSP → NUP:** compress plaintext NSPs created by NSP Box.

releases.body:
## 1.0.47 (2026-11)

### New
- Stick anti dead zone, in Settings, Controls, Stick range, and for each
  game in its own Controls. Many Xbox games ignore the first part of a
  stick's travel themselves (they were made for the original controller's
  loose sticks), so even with the dead zone at 0 a small push does
  nothing. In Chicago Enforcer, for example, the view doesn't turn at all
  until the stick is about a third of the way over. The anti dead zone
  makes the smallest push past the dead zone start at that amount, so
  the game reacts straight away. Both stick boxes on the Stick range
  screen draw it as a red disc, next to the dead zone's grey ring.
- A game's Controls now have its own sticks (dead zone, anti dead zone,
  range, shape) and triggers, so each game can be set apart from the
  global settings. Thanks to crashmidnick25 for the report (#84).

releases.name: xbased 1.0.46
releases.body:
## 1.0.46 (2026-11)

### Fixes
- Less audio stutter on Linux in games with a lot of sound going on,
  like Forza Motorsport's races. The emulated sound chip's voices were
  split between the audio thread and a helper thread, and on Linux
  waking the helper and waiting for it 1500 times a second cost more
  than the work it took over. In a Forza race the audio thread was busy
  about three times as much on Linux as on Windows on the same machine,
  and on slower laptops it couldn't keep up. On Linux the audio thread
  now does the voices itself, which takes it from around 20% busy to
  around 7% in that race. Windows keeps the helper, which pays off
  there. Thanks to saultsomy-jpg for the report and the detailed log
  (#82).

releases.name: xbased 1.0.45
releases.body:
## 1.0.45 (2026-11)

### Fixes
- Chicago Enforcer no longer freezes when starting a new game. Its
  loading screen works with events it opens by name, and the emulator
  had no way to open an object by name, so it stopped right there. Named
  events, semaphores and mutants are now supported, and a name goes away
  with the last handle to it, as on the console, since the next loading
  screen waits for exactly that. The game now gets through both loads
  of the first chapter and plays. Thanks to P1Login for the report (#56).

releases.name: xbased 1.0.44
releases.body:
## 1.0.44 (2026-11)

### Fixes
- The updater on Windows no longer gives up on an update that unpacked
  fine. It unpacks the new version with Windows' own tar, and on some
  Windows 10 machines tar reported an error even though every file came
  out right, so the updater stopped and opened the releases page
  instead. Now, when tar reports an error, the updater checks every
  file of the package against the download (its name and size) and
  carries on if they're all there. Thanks to shadowflash for the report
  (#76).

releases.name: xbased 1.0.43
releases.body:
## 1.0.43 (2026-11)

### Fixes
- Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge no longer goes back to the
  dashboard as it starts. Some games check that the disc is an original
  by reading its security sector, which lives in a part of the disc that
  disc images don't include, and the emulator handed back zeros. The
  emulated DVD drive now makes a security sector that passes the game's
  check (the right time stamp and checksum, signed with a key of
  xbased's own, which the emulated console uses as its public key). The
  game now boots and plays. Thanks to BlueDragon992 for the report (#80).

releases.name: v2.5.0
releases.body:
## Highlights

- **Disk images are kept unmodified with a save directory.** With `-saveDir`, what the software writes goes to an overlay file there and the image is only read. Overlays store only the tracks or blocks written and are tied to a checksum of their image. This also makes writable the disks that could not be written before: inside a zip or gzip, loaded from a URL, or embedded in the executable.
- **DOS 3.3 boots in five seconds.** The Disk II motor keeps turning for about a second after the drive is turned off, like the 556 timer of the real controller, and the data latch no longer reads the same nibble twice. DOS no longer waits for the motor on every access: a DOS 3.3 boot takes 5.4 million cycles instead of 36 million.
- **A libretro core** runs izapple2 inside RetroArch and the other libretro frontends, with diskette swapping from M3U playlists and saves as overlays. It is built from source and is not in the release archives.
